transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-08-17 14:30 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SRE), Anya Kaur (Silverpine Head of ML), Diego Ruiz (Silverpine Cloud Architect), Marta Green (Silverpine Security Lead), Tom Becker (Silverpine CTO)

Summary:
Quick kickoff focused on security gating for a POC, what benchmarks Silverpine needs (latency/throughput), how Redwood will run benchmarks (hosted vs dedicated), and timelines/next steps. Heavy emphasis on SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML with Okta, RBAC model, audit logs + KMS encryption.

Topics Covered:
- Security artifacts (SOC 2, ISO 27001) and evidence cadence
- SSO/SAML integration approach (Okta) and SCIM provisioning
- RBAC model and token-level access controls
- Audit logging, log retention, and export to customer's SIEM
- Deployment options for pilot: hosted with VPC peering vs private dedicated
- Benchmark plan: latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput, batch sizing, token distribution
- Acceptance criteria and timeline

Action items (not exhaustive, also in metadata): see action_items field

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to run through the pilot gates and a rough benchmark plan, make sure security checks are covered. I think we're set for 45 minutes if that's ok.
[00:17] Tom Becker: Yep that's perfect, thanks Maya. Quick intro, I'm Tom, CTO, Marta runs security, Diego handles infra, Anya owns the ML use-cases.
[00:29] Maya Chen: Great, super. Liam and Ravi from our side are on the line for technical details.
[00:35] Liam Ortega: Hi all, I'll pick up on the benchmark and integration questions.
[00:40] Anya Kaur: We sent over a spreadsheet with a sample prompt set and token histograms, did you see that?
[00:46] Diego Ruiz: Yeah I uploaded it to the shared drive, you should have access.
[00:50] Maya Chen: We got it, thanks. That will drive the throughput and p99 goals. Quick question for Silverpine: what's your gating criteria for the POC to be considered successful?
[01:05] Anya Kaur: Functionally we need response quality to be within our eval metrics — F1-ish for our extraction tasks — but from infra/security we need low latency at scale and SOC2 evidence. Also single-sign on, RBAC, and audit trails.
[01:19] Marta Green: To be explicit: SOC 2 Type II or equivalent, ISO27001 summary, SSO via Okta using SAML or OIDC, SCIM for provisioning if possible, RBAC with role separation, encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS, and audit logs exported to Splunk with retention for 12 months.
[01:40] Ravi Patel: Got it. For KMS we support integrating customer KMS via our private deployment; for hosted we can support envelope encryption with CMKs and rotate keys as agreed. There can be small differences in the workflow.
[01:57] Diego Ruiz: That raises the question — are you proposing hosted with VPC peering or an on-prem/private deployment for the pilot?
[02:06] Liam Ortega: Two main paths: quick path is hosted with private VPC peering and allowlist IPs and an IAM service account for the benchmark; the more locked-down path is Redwood Private deployed into your VPC or on-prem. The benchmark numbers are usually comparable but private gives you full KMS and logging control.
[02:26] Tom Becker: We prefer to start with hosted + peering to move faster, unless there's a blocker. Marta, thoughts?
[02:33] Marta Green: Hosted with peering is acceptable for the pilot if we get the SOC2 docs and a contractual commitment on log export and key management posture. Also we need RBAC controls so platform users can be scoped to environments and models.
[02:48] Maya Chen: On the SOC2/ISO docs, we'll send the latest SOC2 Type II attestation and an ISO27001 summary tonight. Those are standard artifacts we share.
[02:58] Anya Kaur: Great — can you also include any third-party penetration test summaries or a short security FAQ?
[03:05] Maya Chen: Yep, we'll include a concise FAQ and the penetration test high-levels.
[03:12] Liam Ortega: For SSO — Okta SAML is our most common integration. We support both SAML and OIDC, and SCIM for user provisioning. For the pilot, SCIM can be optional; we can do manual mapping if you prefer.
[03:28] Diego Ruiz: SCIM would save us time if you support group sync so roles line up with RBAC policies.
[03:33] Liam Ortega: Absolutely, group sync -> RBAC mapping is supported. We'll share the RBAC matrix template.
[03:39] Marta Green: Regarding logs: we need immutable audit logs for admin activity and token access, also model invocation metadata (model id, version, route, latency, request id). Can you stream those to Splunk or S3?
[03:55] Ravi Patel: Yes, we can stream logs to customer S3 buckets or push to HTTP endpoints; Splunk ingest is common. Retention policy can be set on your side, we can also keep short-term copies for 30 days for troubleshooting.
[04:10] Anya Kaur: What about pseudonymization? Some of our prompts contain PHI in test data. We need to ensure logging doesn't capture full prompt text.
[04:19] Liam Ortega: We can redact prompt bodies from logs on request, and keep hashes or metadata for troubleshooting. For the pilot we usually agree on a sanitized dataset for benchmarks to avoid PHI entirely.
[04:33] Tom Becker: Benchmarks — what metrics should we expect and what is a realistic target?
[04:38] Liam Ortega: Based on similar workloads: p50 ~ 50–80ms, p95 ~ 120–180ms for short prompts (<128 tokens) on dedicated GPU-backed routes. For hosted pooled routes numbers can be slightly higher depending on burst. Throughput target depends on batching: with continuous batching and small batch sizes you can get ~200–500 tokens/sec per GPU core equivalent, but we'll size based on your QPS.
[05:01] Anya Kaur: Our baseline is 300 QPS of short prompts, 90% under 128 tokens. We want p95 < 200ms in steady state.
[05:12] Liam Ortega: That's reasonable. For the pilot we'll run a synthetic two-hour run that mimics your token distribution and ramp to your target QPS. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, tail latency, error rate, and cost estimate per million tokens.
[05:26] Diego Ruiz: Cost estimate is important for us — can Redwood provide token cost and also the delta if we use quantized models or smaller model variants as fallbacks?
[05:36] Maya Chen: Yes we can provide a cost model: hosted per-token pricing, and an estimate for dedicated capacity. We'll show cost vs latency tradeoffs and fallback policies.
[05:45] Marta Green: For acceptance criteria, we need explicit numbers: function correctness (accuracy metric threshold from Anya), latency p95 <= 200ms, error rate < 0.1% over the run, audit logs exported and searchable, and SSO/RBAC tested.
[06:02] Anya Kaur: Correct — add also that model outputs must not regress versus baseline by more than 2% in our eval metric.
[06:09] Maya Chen: We'll draft an acceptance criteria doc and share.
[06:14] Diego Ruiz: On timelines — when can we run the benchmark? We need to coordinate maintenance windows and firewall rules.
[06:21] Liam Ortega: If we get the test VPC creds and the workload manifest by Aug 20, we can schedule benchmark the week of Aug 30. The two-hour run plus follow-up analysis typically gets you a report within 48 hours.
[06:34] Tom Becker: That works. We need to confirm Azure vs AWS region availability — Diego will confirm which region we want to test in.
[06:42] Diego Ruiz: We'll likely choose eu-west-2, but I'll confirm.
[06:46] Marta Green: A couple of nitty-gritty items: SAML signing algorithms, assertion lifetime, session timeout, SCIM group naming conventions, and service account IP allowlists.
[06:57] Liam Ortega: We'll include an Okta config sample. For SAML we support SHA256 signatures and adjustable assertion lifetime. Session timeouts are configurable. IP allowlists and mutual TLS is available for the peering endpoints.
[07:09] Anya Kaur: How about model version pinning and rollbacks during the pilot — we need deterministic behavior for evaluation.
[07:17] Ravi Patel: You can pin to a model version for the pilot. We'll also give you a snapshot of model weights (metadata) and a rollout plan; automatic rollbacks can be disabled for the duration of the POC.
[07:28] Tom Becker: Any surprises we should know about for private deployment later?
[07:33] Maya Chen: For private deployments there's an installation window — usually a week for infra and network prep plus one day for install and testing. Ops and security usually want a deeper review but for POC we stick to hosted+peering to get data quickly.
[07:46] Marta Green: One more: auditability around prompts and who invoked what — we might need lineage to meet compliance audits.
[07:54] Liam Ortega: We can provide request-level metadata including a hashed prompt id, user id (or role), timestamp, model id/version, and latency. Full prompt text can be redacted as requested.
[08:06] Anya Kaur: Good. Also we want to run 2-3 A/B tests across model variants as part of the POC — does that complicate benchmarking?
[08:15] Liam Ortega: Not at all, we can do parallel test routes and compare results. We recommend running each variant for a sufficient sample to get stable p95 numbers; we can automate traffic split and report on quality metrics per variant.
[08:29] Diego Ruiz: Security/legal: can you share standard contract language for data processing and subprocessors?
[08:35] Maya Chen: Yes we'll share the DPA and subprocessor list. For the pilot we typically do a limited DPA addendum.
[08:42] Tom Becker: Okay let's recap next steps.
[08:45] Maya Chen: Recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO docs + pen test summary; Liam will send RBAC template and Okta sample; Diego to provide workload + region; Marta confirm KMS + log retention; schedule benchmark week of Aug 30. I'll put the acceptance criteria doc in near-term.
[09:02] Marta Green: One ask — can we get an on-call contact during the benchmark?
[09:06] Ravi Patel: Yes, we'll provide an escalation contact and Slack channel during the run.
[09:10] Anya Kaur: Great, that should cover it.
[09:14] Tom Becker: Thanks everyone, look forward to the docs.
[09:17] Maya Chen: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the action items.

End of meeting.
